At Hedong a storm drove his heavy transport across to the north bank; the 'braided caitiffs' (Suolu, the Tuoba Wei) captured the vessel and stripped its stores.
索虜 is the Southern dynasties' term for the Tuoba Wei, not the Di people.
When they reached Hedong, a violent wind drove Fan's heavy ship across to the north bank; the Di barbarians of the north seized the ship and took its equipment.
When they reached Hedong, a violent wind drove Fan's heavy ship across to the north bank; the braided caitiffs (Suolu) seized the ship and took its equipment.

In the first year of Jingping under Emperor Shao, Fan was dismissed for guarding the Eastern Palace and opening the side gate, but soon had his post restored.

Fan's fourteenth son Zunshi had served on Zang Zhi's staff as General Who Pacifies the Distance; he left office, went home, and plotted with Kong Xixian. Because of Fan's service, the emperor would not expose the affair and had Jiangzhou arrest and execute Zunshi on a pretext.

Fan's fourteenth son Zunshi had served as an aide to Zang Zhi, General Who Pacifies the Distance; he left office, went home, and plotted with Kong Xixian. Because of Fan's service, the emperor would not expose the affair and had Jiangzhou arrest and execute Zunshi on a pretext.
臧質寧遠參軍: Zunshi was an aide (參軍) to Zang Zhi, who held the title 寧遠 (General Who Pacifies the Distance); Zunshi was not the general.

On the western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi, the emperor sent Tan Daoji and Zhu Chao-shi with infantry and cavalry from Xiangyang. Qianzhi, then administrator of Jiangxia, marched from Yucheng, encamped at Sanlian, bridged the river, and stockpiled grain for the relief force.

On the western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi and Lu Zongzhi, the emperor sent Tan Daoji and Zhu Chao-shi with infantry and cavalry from Xiangyang. Qianzhi, then administrator of Jiangxia, marched from Yuncheng, encamped at Sanlian, bridged the river, and stockpiled grain for the relief force.
溳城: 溳 is read yún.

縣瓠 is the city of Xuanhu (seat of Runan), not a county named Hu. 偽殿中尚書任城公乞地真: a Wei (not Rouran) Palace Minister and Duke of Rencheng; the translation also drops the titles.

When the Founding Emperor campaigned west against Sima Xiuzhi, Lu Zongzhi, and others, he sent the aides Tan Daoji and Zhu Chao-shi with infantry and cavalry out from Xiangyang; Qianzhi was then Administrator of Jiangxia and led the commandery and prefectural forces out from Yucheng, encamped at Sanlian, built a bridge, and gathered grain to await them.

When the Founding Emperor campaigned west against Sima Xiuzhi, Lu Zongzhi, and others, he sent the aides Tan Daoji and Zhu Chao-shi with infantry and cavalry out from Xiangyang; Qianzhi was then Administrator of Jiangxia and led the commandery and prefectural forces out from Yuncheng, encamped at Sanlian, built a bridge, and gathered grain to await them.

征虜 is the title General Who Conquers the Caitiffs (征虜將軍).
In spring of the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia the Rouran ruler Tuoba Tao led a great army against Runan. Emperor Taizu sent relief forces, with Kangzu in overall command of the vanguard.
In spring of the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia the Tuoba Wei ruler Tuoba Tao led a great army against Runan. Emperor Taizu sent relief forces, with Kangzu in overall command of the vanguard.

The emperor considered that righteous partisans were rising everywhere north of the Yellow River; if the army halted for a full year, it would dampen their zeal for the cause, and he did not agree.

Kangzu was still several tens of li from Shouyang when the Wei Prince of Yongchang, Kurenzhen, overtook him at Yuwu with eighty thousand cavalry from Chang'an.
虜 here are the Tuoba Wei (Tuoba Tao's army), not the Rouran.

Du Daojun and the Wei pretender-court minister Fulian came to relieve Que'ao; Huzhi drove them off and the enemy marched east.
偽尚書 is a minister of the Wei ('false') court; the Rouran are not involved.

Shengzhi had courage and strength; he was first an army aide and commander of guards on the Pacification Army staff of the Prince of Changsha, Yixin; in suppressing bandits in Qiao commandery, seventy bandits with horse and foot on the west of the county fled into deep thickets; Shengzhi advanced alone with bared body and personally beheaded fifty-eight of them.

Yixuan brought a great army to Liangshan and locked in stalemate with Wang Xuemo.
Yixuan brought a great army to Liangshan and locked in stalemate with Wang Xuanmo.

His younger brother Xunzhi was fierce and bold with great physical strength; the arch-criminal had long heard his name and made him deputy to the General Who Assists the State, Zhang Jian.
